title: Cisco Multicloud Defense Egress Filter Volume
exclusions: Counts URL, FQDN, and SNI filter events only. The add-on publishes no field list for these sourcetypes, so allow and deny are not separated.
evidence: Hourly event counts by sourcetype for 30 days.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Generate a test event that Multicloud Defense records as one of `cisco:multicloud:defense:urlfilter`, `cisco:multicloud:defense:fqdnfilter`, `cisco:multicloud:defense:fqdn_resolve`, `cisco:multicloud:defense:sni`. The next hour shows a count above zero for that sourcetype.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Stop the HEC export from Security Cloud Control. The next hour is zero for every sourcetype in this search.

dataSources: `index=cisco_multicloud_defense` sourcetypes `cisco:multicloud:defense:urlfilter`, `cisco:multicloud:defense:fqdnfilter`, `cisco:multicloud:defense:fqdn_resolve`, `cisco:multicloud:defense:sni`. Cisco Security Cloud (7404) receives Multicloud Defense over HEC. The user guide's example input sets `sourcetype=cisco:multicloud:defense` and `index=cisco_multicloud_defense`. Splunk's Cisco app navigator lists the more specific sourcetypes used here. No field list is published.

description: Counts Cisco Multicloud Defense URL, FQDN, and SNI filter events per hour, one series per sourcetype. The add-on publishes these sourcetypes and no field names, so the search counts events instead of reading action or address fields.
value: Cloud workloads calling out to blocked destinations are how a compromised instance phones home. This count shows the egress-filter logs are still arriving so that call is visible.
implementation: Create the Multicloud Defense HEC input in Cisco Security Cloud with index cisco_multicloud_defense. Chart these sourcetypes per hour and alert when all of them are zero during a staffed hour.
visualization: Column chart of event count per hour, split by sourcetype.

references.title: Cisco Security Cloud App for Splunk User Guide
Splunk Cisco app navigator: onboarded sourcetypes

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Quiet gateways** — a lab gateway with no traffic produces zeros. Compare with the gateway's own traffic graph before paging.

**Suppression:** alert when every sourcetype in this search is zero during staffed hours.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, Splunkbase 7404) on the search heads and on the heavy forwarder or Splunk Cloud Inputs Data Manager that runs its modular inputs.
• Multicloud Defense sending logs to this HEC token, configured from Security Cloud Control, as the user guide describes.
• An index for this data (this page uses `cisco_multicloud_defense`) and a role with `srchIndexesAllowed` on it for the SOC.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
• In Cisco Security Cloud open Application Setup, choose the Multicloud Defense card, and create an input. Set the index to `cisco_multicloud_defense`.
• The input writes `sourcetype IN ("cisco:multicloud:defense:urlfilter", "cisco:multicloud:defense:fqdnfilter", "cisco:multicloud:defense:fqdn_resolve", "cisco:multicloud:defense:sni")`.
• Confirm events arrive with the search in Step 2, over the last hour. A count above zero means the input is writing.

Step 2 — Create the search
```spl
index=cisco_multicloud_defense sourcetype IN ("cisco:multicloud:defense:urlfilter", "cisco:multicloud:defense:fqdnfilter", "cisco:multicloud:defense:fqdn_resolve", "cisco:multicloud:defense:sni") earliest=-24h
| timechart span=1h count by sourcetype
```

Understanding this SPL
• `timechart count by sourcetype` keeps each log type visible. A missing series means that log type stopped.
• Action, address, and rule fields are not documented, so they are not used.

Step 3 — Validate
• In Security Cloud Control, open the Multicloud Defense logs for the same hour and log type. Events there and nothing here means the HEC export is down.

• Confirm in the vendor console that the same hour shows the same kind of event before trusting a zero or a spike.

Step 4 — Operationalize
• Put the panel on the SOC dashboard for Multicloud Defense and refresh it hourly.
• Alert when the count drops to zero during a staffed period, which means the input stopped, and throttle for 4 hours.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• HTTP 401 or 403 on the HEC token: the token on the Security Cloud Control side does not match the input.
• Parent sourcetype cisco:multicloud:defense arrives but these specific sourcetypes do not: the gateway is not emitting that log type. Enable it on the gateway before expecting this panel to move.
• No data for this sourcetype, with an input error in the Cisco Security Cloud log, means the credential or token is incorrect.
grandmaExplanation: We count the outbound filter records Cisco sends each hour, so we still see cloud servers trying to reach blocked sites.
